monuments.fact: Transformed between 1772 and 1795 for King Stanisław August Poniatowski into a Neoclassical villa afloat on an artificial island in the Royal Baths Park, hosting the famous Thursday Dinners of the Polish Enlightenment.

monuments.architect: Cantilevered Steel-Glass Station Hall (Arseniusz Romanowicz, 1975) & 310m Varso Tower (Foster + Partners, 2022)
monuments.architecturalStyle: Cantilevered Steel-Glass Station Hall (Arseniusz Romanowicz, 1975) & 310m Varso Tower (Foster + Partners, 2022)
monuments.fact: Pairing Arseniusz Romanowicz’s bold 1975 winged modernist railway terminal above the Cross-City Line with Foster + Partners’ 310-meter Varso Tower (2022)—the tallest skyscraper in the European Union.

monuments.name: Wilanów Palace — The Polish Versailles (Pałac w Wilanowie)
monuments.localName: Pałac Króla Jana III w Wilanowie
monuments.architect: Baroque Cour d’Honneur, Twin Copper-Helmeted Towers & Gilded Sundials (Augustyn Locci, 1696)
monuments.architecturalStyle: Baroque Cour d’Honneur, Twin Copper-Helmeted Towers & Gilded Sundials (Augustyn Locci, 1696)
monuments.fact: Built between 1677 and 1696 for King Jan III Sobieski after the Relief of Vienna, Wilanów blends Italian villa rustica, French Baroque palatial wings, and Polish Sarmatian courtly reliefs that survived WWII intact.
